fixtures.rationale: Three chained ternaries build a tier label; a lookup table or an if/else chain would express the same four-way choice without stacking conditional operators.
The reduce rebuilds an object keyed by id one entry at a time; Object.fromEntries(items.map(...)) would build the same index directly.
The pattern has no alternation or character classes; it is a fixed prefix, so url.startsWith('https:') says the same thing without a regex engine.
Double bitwise NOT truncates toward zero as a side effect of two's-complement arithmetic; Math.trunc says what is meant.
Double negation coerces to boolean as a trick; Boolean(user.email) or a comparison against undefined/null says the same thing plainly.
eval runs arbitrary source as code; a dedicated expression parser or a fixed set of supported operations would meet the same requirement without that surface.
A single-level ternary is already the plainest form of a two-way choice; there is nothing to simplify further.
The reduce folds to a scalar sum with a numeric initial value, which is exactly what reduce is for; no map/filter/Object.fromEntries call replaces it.
The pattern uses real character classes and repetition to validate an email shape; no single string method expresses that.
This is a real bit-flag test against a named flag constant, which is exactly what the bitwise AND operator is for; there is no plainer equivalent.
The reduce hand-rolls grouping into a Map; Map.groupBy or Object.groupBy expresses the same grouping directly without the manual get-then-set dance.
The filename matches the default test file pattern, so the rule produces no candidates at all regardless of its contents.
